# Forum digest: "A few statement rows get the wrong category or payee"

Collected from a user support thread. In every case the money moved correctly;
only the derived label is wrong - the category, the sub-tag, or the counterparty
name - and only on a handful of unusual row shapes. Three representative posts,
lightly anonymized, then a maintainer note.

---

**mango_saver** -
> Two rows on this month's statement look off. A credit whose reference note is
> nothing but a long all-numeric string used to show up as a cheque deposit and
> now it just reads as a generic transfer. Separately, my salary credit - whose
> narration is a bare numeric code and nothing else - has stopped picking up the
> salary sub-tag it always had.

**rk_ontheroad** -
> Mine is the name field, not the category. On transfers whose narration opens
> with a direction word ahead of the name, the counterparty now comes back
> empty or wrong. Ordinary transfers that don't open that way are still
> labelled fine; it's only that leading-keyword narration style.

**auditlens** -
> Bill transfers that use a slash-delimited reference are pulling the wrong
> payee. When the reference is laid out as four fields - a type, a sub-type, a
> numeric reference, then the payee name as the final field - the app is lifting
> the numeric reference into the name column instead of the actual name sitting
> at the end.

---

**Maintainer note.** Consolidating these. Each one sits on an edge form that
everyday rows rarely produce, which is why routine activity looks healthy and
nothing tripped in review. On top of the three above we reproduced one more in
the same family: an offsetting credit that arrives immediately after its
matching debit is being recorded as a bounce rather than the reversal it
really is.

The labeling logic is deterministic - the same row always maps to the same
label - so each complaint can be recreated from a single synthetic row and
chased to the exact rule at fault. Expect the faults to sit on boundaries and
structural offsets inside otherwise-correct rules, not in the common paths.

**Ask for engineering:** restore correct handling so these edge rows label
correctly again, without shifting any row that already comes out right. Success
is that the situations described here enrich correctly and nothing that is
currently correct changes.
I'll start by exploring the codebase to understand the structure and find the labeling logic.

Reproduce issue 1: all-numeric reference credit -> cheque deposit
Reproduce issue 2: bare numeric narration salary credit -> salary sub-tag
Reproduce issue 3: leading direction keyword narration -> counterparty name
Reproduce issue 4: slash-delimited 4-field bill transfer -> payee is last field
Reproduce issue 5: offsetting credit right after debit -> reversal not bounce
Fix each root cause and verify no regression on correct rows

import pandas as pd

from categorizationapp.BankScripts.HDFC import categorize_HDFC_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.ICICI import categorize_ICICI_transactions
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts.Purpose import purpose
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts.CleanName import clean_names


def frame(rows):
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    for c in ["remark", "description"]:
        if c not in df:
            df[c] = ""
    if "balanceAfterTransaction" not in df:
        df["balanceAfterTransaction"] = 10000.0
    if "transactionDate" not in df:
        df["transactionDate"] = "01/01/2022"
    return df


def show(title, df, cols=("description", "remark", "type", "amount", "transactionCategory",
                          "transactionSubcategory", "partyName")):
    print("=" * 30, title)
    print(df[list(cols)].to_string())
    print()


# ---------- Issue 1: long all-numeric remark credit -> CHEQUE_DEPOSIT ----------
df = frame([
    {"description": "SOME NARRATION", "remark": "0000000000012345", "type": "CREDIT", "amount": 5000.0},
    {"description": "SOME NARRATION", "remark": "000000000001234", "type": "CREDIT", "amount": 5000.0},
])
out = categorize_HDFC_transactions(df.copy(), "SAVING")
show("issue1 HDFC numeric remark credit", out)

# ---------- Issue 2: bare numeric narration salary credit ----------
df = frame([
    {"description": "123456", "remark": "N012345678901234", "type": "CREDIT", "amount": 50000.0},
])
out = categorize_HDFC_transactions(df.copy(), "SAVING")
show("issue2 HDFC bare numeric narration (SAVING)", out)

# ---------- Issue 3: ICICI leading direction keyword transfer ----------
df = frame([
    {"description": "TRFR TO:RAMESH KUMAR", "type": "DEBIT", "amount": 2500.0},
    {"description": "TRFR FROM:SUNIL SHARMA", "type": "CREDIT", "amount": 2500.0},
    {"description": "TRF/1234567/ORDINARY NAME", "type": "DEBIT", "amount": 100.0},
])
out = categorize_ICICI_transactions(df.copy(), "SAVING")
show("issue3 ICICI TRFR TO/FROM", out)

# ---------- Issue 4: ICICI BIL/INFT 4 field slash reference ----------
df = frame([
    {"description": "BIL/INFT/003456789/ACME UTILITIES", "type": "DEBIT", "amount": 1200.0},
    {"description": "BIL/BPAY/003456789/ACME UTILITIES", "type": "DEBIT", "amount": 1200.0},
    {"description": "BIL/INFT/003456789/REF NOTE/ACME UTILITIES", "type": "DEBIT", "amount": 1200.0},
])
out = categorize_ICICI_transactions(df.copy(), "SAVING")
show("issue4 ICICI BIL/INFT", out)

# ---------- Issue 5: offsetting credit right after matching debit ----------
df = frame([
    {"description": "IMPS-123456789-JOHN DOE-HDFC-XXXXXX", "type": "DEBIT", "amount": 5000.0},
    {"description": "IMPS-123456789-JOHN DOE-HDFC-XXXXXX", "type": "CREDIT", "amount": 5000.0},
])
out = categorize_HDFC_transactions(df.copy(), "SAVING")
show("issue5 HDFC reversal pair", out)

df = frame([
    {"description": "ACH D- SOMECO-1234", "type": "DEBIT", "amount": 5000.0},
    {"description": "ACH D- SOMECO-1234", "type": "CREDIT", "amount": 5000.0},
])
out = categorize_HDFC_transactions(df.copy(), "SAVING")
show("issue5 control: non-transfer bounce pair (should stay AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE)", out)

import pandas as pd

from categorizationapp.BankScripts.HDFC import categorize_HDFC_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.ICICI import categorize_ICICI_transactions

PASS, FAIL = "PASS", "FAIL"
results = []


def frame(rows):
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    for c in ("remark", "description"):
        if c not in df:
            df[c] = ""
    df["remark"] = df["remark"].fillna("")
    if "balanceAfterTransaction" not in df:
        df["balanceAfterTransaction"] = 10000.0
    return df


def check(name, got, expected):
    status = PASS if got == expected else FAIL
    results.append((status, name, got, expected))


def hdfc(rows, accountType="SAVING"):
    return categorize_HDFC_transactions(frame(rows), accountType)


def icici(rows, accountType="SAVING"):
    return categorize_ICICI_transactions(frame(rows), accountType)


# ---- Issue 1: HDFC credit whose ref-no is a long all-numeric string -> CHEQUE_DEPOSIT
out = hdfc([{"description": "SOME NARRATION", "remark": "0000000000012345",
             "type": "CREDIT", "amount": 5000.0}])
check("1 numeric ref credit -> CHEQUE_DEPOSIT", out.transactionCategory[0], "CHEQUE_DEPOSIT")

# control: 16-digit ref that is not zero padded stays a plain transfer with name kept
out = hdfc([{"description": "SOME NARRATION", "remark": "1234567890123456",
             "type": "CREDIT", "amount": 5000.0}])
check("1c non zero-padded ref stays TRANSFER", out.transactionCategory[0], "TRANSFER")
check("1c non zero-padded ref keeps name", out.partyName[0], "Some Narration")

# control: same ref shape but a debit is untouched
out = hdfc([{"description": "SOME NARRATION", "remark": "0000000000012345",
             "type": "DEBIT", "amount": 5000.0}])
check("1c debit unaffected", out.transactionCategory[0], "TRANSFER")

# ---- Issue 2: HDFC salary credit whose narration is a bare numeric code
out = hdfc([{"description": "123456", "remark": "N012345678901234",
             "type": "CREDIT", "amount": 50000.0}])
check("2 bare numeric narration -> SALARY", out.transactionSubcategory[0], "SALARY")
check("2 category still TRANSFER", out.transactionCategory[0], "TRANSFER")

# controls: not a saving account / debit / not a bare numeric code
out = hdfc([{"description": "123456", "remark": "", "type": "CREDIT", "amount": 50000.0}], "CURRENT")
check("2c CURRENT account not tagged salary", out.transactionSubcategory[0], "")
out = hdfc([{"description": "123456", "remark": "", "type": "DEBIT", "amount": 50000.0}])
check("2c debit not tagged salary", out.transactionSubcategory[0], "")
out = hdfc([{"description": "1234567", "remark": "", "type": "CREDIT", "amount": 50000.0}])
check("2c 7-digit narration not tagged salary", out.transactionSubcategory[0], "")

# ---- Issue 3: ICICI transfer narration opening with a direction word
out = icici([{"description": "TRFR TO:RAMESH KUMAR", "type": "DEBIT", "amount": 2500.0},
             {"description": "TRFR FROM:SUNIL SHARMA", "type": "CREDIT", "amount": 2500.0}])
check("3 TRFR TO: name", out.partyName[0], "Ramesh Kumar")
check("3 TRFR FROM: name", out.partyName[1], "Sunil Sharma")

# control: ordinary transfer narration unchanged
out = icici([{"description": "TRF/1234567/ORDINARY NAME", "type": "DEBIT", "amount": 100.0}])
check("3c ordinary TRF/ name", out.partyName[0], "1234567")

# ---- Issue 4: ICICI slash delimited bill reference, payee is the last field
out = icici([{"description": "BIL/INFT/003456789/ACME UTILITIES", "type": "DEBIT", "amount": 1200.0},
             {"description": "BIL/INFT/12345/ACME UTILITIES", "type": "DEBIT", "amount": 1200.0}])
check("4 BIL/INFT payee (long ref)", out.partyName[0], "Acme Utilities")
check("4 BIL/INFT payee (short ref)", out.partyName[1], "Acme Utilities")

# controls: sibling BIL forms keep working
out = icici([{"description": "BIL/BPAY/003456789/ACME UTILITIES", "type": "DEBIT", "amount": 1200.0},
             {"description": "BIL/INFT/003456789/REF NOTE/ACME UTILITIES", "type": "DEBIT", "amount": 1200.0},
             {"description": "BIL/ONL/003456789/ACME UTILITIES", "type": "DEBIT", "amount": 1200.0}])
check("4c BIL/BPAY payee", out.partyName[0], "Acme Utilities")
check("4c BIL/INFT 5-field payee", out.partyName[1], "Acme Utilities")
check("4c BIL/ONL payee", out.partyName[2], "Acme Utilities")

# ---- Issue 5: offsetting credit immediately after its matching debit
out = hdfc([{"description": "NEFT PAYMENT TO XYZ TRADERS", "type": "DEBIT", "amount": 7500.0},
            {"description": "NEFT PAYMENT TO XYZ TRADERS", "type": "CREDIT", "amount": 7500.0}])
check("5 offsetting credit -> REVERSAL", out.transactionCategory[1], "REVERSAL")
check("5 original debit untouched", out.transactionCategory[0], "TRANSFER")

# control: a matching pair without a transfer keyword is still a bounce
out = hdfc([{"description": "MANDATE PAYMENT ABC", "type": "DEBIT", "amount": 7500.0},
            {"description": "MANDATE PAYMENT ABC", "type": "CREDIT", "amount": 7500.0}])
check("5c non-transfer pair stays AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE", out.transactionCategory[1], "AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE")

# control: credit not directly after the debit is not a reversal
out = hdfc([{"description": "NEFT PAYMENT TO XYZ TRADERS", "type": "DEBIT", "amount": 7500.0},
            {"description": "SOMETHING ELSE", "type": "DEBIT", "amount": 10.0},
            {"description": "NEFT PAYMENT TO XYZ TRADERS", "type": "CREDIT", "amount": 7500.0}])
check("5c non-adjacent credit not REVERSAL", out.transactionCategory[2], "TRANSFER")

# control: differing amounts are not a reversal
out = hdfc([{"description": "NEFT PAYMENT TO XYZ TRADERS", "type": "DEBIT", "amount": 7500.0},
            {"description": "NEFT PAYMENT TO XYZ TRADERS", "type": "CREDIT", "amount": 500.0}])
check("5c different amount not REVERSAL", out.transactionCategory[1], "TRANSFER")

for status, name, got, expected in results:
    print(f"{status}  {name}: got={got!r} expected={expected!r}")
print()
print(f"{sum(1 for r in results if r[0] == PASS)}/{len(results)} passed")

arguments.content:
"""Adjacent-pair corpus: exercises the neighbour-dependent REVERSAL / BOUNCE rules."""
import json
import sys

import pandas as pd

from categorizationapp.BankScripts.HDFC import categorize_HDFC_transactions

DESCS = [
    "NEFT PAYMENT TO XYZ TRADERS",   # transfer keyword, no earlier rule match
    "SOME UPI ISH ENTRY",
    "MANDATE PAYMENT ABC",           # no transfer keyword -> bounce
    "IMPS-123456789-JOHN DOE-HDFC",  # matched by the IMPS rule earlier
    "ACH D- SOMECO-1234",
    "SOME NARRATION",
    "PLAIN NAME",
]

rows = []
for d in DESCS:
    for d2 in DESCS:
        for same_amt in (True, False):
            for order in ((("DEBIT", d), ("CREDIT", d2)),
                          (("CREDIT", d), ("DEBIT", d2)),
                          (("DEBIT", d), ("DEBIT", d2)),
                          (("CREDIT", d), ("CREDIT", d2))):
                for i, (t, desc) in enumerate(order):
                    rows.append({"description": desc, "remark": "", "type": t,
                                 "amount": 5000.0 if (same_amt or i == 0) else 900.0,
                                 "balanceAfterTransaction": 10000.0,
                                 "transactionDate": "05/01/2022"})

df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
out = categorize_HDFC_transactions(df.copy(), "SAVING")
recs = out[["description", "type", "amount", "transactionCategory",
            "transactionSubcategory", "partyName"]].to_dict(orient="records")
json.dump(recs, open(sys.argv[1], "w"), indent=1, default=str)
print("wrote", sys.argv[1], len(recs), "rows")

steps.message:
All five reported situations traced to five one-token faults in two bank rule sets, each reproduced from a single synthetic row before fixing.

## Fixes

**`BankScripts/HDFC.py`**

1. **Cheque deposit on an all-numeric reference** (`HDFC.py:100`) — the rule required `remark.str.len().eq(15)` while its regex `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` needs 16 characters, so the condition was unsatisfiable and every such credit fell through to the `TRANSFER` default. Changed to `eq(16)`, consistent with the other two remark rules in the same file (`^N[0-9]{15}$`, `^[0-9]{16}$` — HDFC's ref field is fixed-width 16).

2. **Salary sub-tag on a bare numeric narration** (`HDFC.py:124`) — the rule tested `accountType=="SAVINGS"`, but the caller and every other rule in the repo use `"SAVING"`, so `^[0-9]{6}$` credits never got `SALARY`. Changed to `"SAVING"`.

3. **Reversal vs bounce on an offsetting credit** (`HDFC.py:98`) — the `REVERSAL` rule compared `description` against `shift(periods=2)` while its type/amount checks used `shift(periods=1)`. The genuine adjacent pair therefore missed `REVERSAL` and fell into the next rule (`AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`), and unrelated rows two positions apart got spurious reversals. Changed to `shift(periods=1)` (matches the identical ICICI rule).

**`BankScripts/ICICI.py`**

4. **Counterparty on direction-keyword narrations** (`ICICI.py:159`) — `py_extract(pat="TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)", index=0)` returned capture group 0, i.e. the direction word itself, so `TRFR TO:` names came back empty (`"To"` is later blanked by the `^[A-Z]{1,2}$` cleanup) and `TRFR FROM:` names came back as `"From"`. Changed to `index=1`.

5. **Payee on slash-delimited bill references** (`ICICI.py:147`) — for `BIL/INFT/<ref>/<payee>` (3 slashes) the rule took `sep_by_(2,3)`, the numeric reference, instead of the final field. Changed to `sep_by_(3,4)`, matching the last-field convention of the sibling `BIL/BPAY`, `BIL/ONL` and `INF/INFT` rules.

## Verification

- 22-assertion check covering all five scenarios plus controls (debits, `CURRENT` accounts, 7-digit narrations, non-adjacent/differing-amount pairs, sibling `BIL/*` forms, ordinary `TRF/` transfers): 22/22 pass.
- Before/after diff over a 6,368-row synthetic corpus (39 HDFC × 7 remarks and 33 ICICI narration forms × both account types, full pipeline incl. `purpose` and `clean_names`): every one of the 488 changed rows is one of the four fixed edge forms; no other row moved.
- Separate 784-row adjacent-pair corpus for the neighbour-dependent rules: 7 changes — the real debit/credit pair becomes `REVERSAL`, and 6 rows lose a reversal label that had been triggered by an unrelated row two positions earlier (the same offset defect).
